output.brief: VA-220 failures are almost certainly a Pellacott valve problem, not an installer or firmware problem. Brenmoor's matched data show Pellacott 2026 valves fail at about the same rate (roughly 41–42 per 1,000) whichever installer or firmware is involved, while Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7. Teardowns show deformed, unseated slide seals. Helium retests of unused warehouse stock show 11% of Pellacott 2026 valves leaking. The independent calibration visit found Pellacott's leak rig out of service since January, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. Certificate values repeat four fixed sequences, some dating from before 2026. So the certificates that lifted Pellacott's score and earned dock-to-stock appear not to reflect real tests. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates, and do not blame or charge back installers. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing. Plan for the line stoppage with Durrant-Hale supply and tested stock. Then require rig logs or witnessed tests in scoring and check other suppliers' records. Still unknown: whether the seal change or the Line 3 move is the physical cause, and whether other suppliers have the same issue. Confidence is high on the main conclusion.
